highlights: Anthropic launched Claude Ship in beta, with Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals taking pull requests through review, fixes and policy-based approval.
OpenAI and Cisco open-sourced Shirudo, which uses eBPF shields to protect running Linux services before a patch lands.
Google DeepMind used Gemini 4 agent teams with Lean verification to improve quantum algorithms, and open-sourced its Lean library.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to review, fix and approve pull requests
items.summary: Claude Ship, available in beta, combines the generally available Code Review with two new agents: PR Steward, which handles failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review feedback but is designed not to approve or merge, and Claude Approvals, which applies an approval policy the team writes as a file in the repository. Developers can try it with the new /ship command in Claude Code, and Anthropic recommends running approvals in observe-only mode before requiring them in branch protection.

evidence.quote: Claude Ship is made up of Code Review , which is already generally available, and two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals.

PR Steward works to keep a PR green, but is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. It jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.

Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios.
For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light.
Developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests with the new /ship command in Claude Code.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo, an eBPF shield runtime for Linux
items.summary: Shirudo lets teams load temporary eBPF shields that block a vulnerable code path on a running Linux system while a patch is prepared; shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading, and a TPM keeps a verifiable record of what was loaded or removed. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without a restart. It is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, giving security teams an open way to let agents draft protections that operators approve.

evidence.quote: OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches.
In a controlled test (opens in a new window) , a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.
Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system.
Shields are cryptographically signed and verified before loading.
Shirudo uses a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) to support a verifiable record of protections being loaded or removed.

Defense at machine speed: OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed.
Shirudo is licensed under BSD 2-Clause, with its BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

items.title: DeepMind uses Gemini 4 agent teams and Lean proofs to speed up quantum algorithms
items.summary: Google DeepMind set separate, independent teams of Gemini 4 agents on well-known quantum algorithms, with every idea verified in Lean before entering a shared notebook. Results include an 11.8× lower computing cost for an inertial confinement fusion circuit (5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits), a 2.5× improvement for Cytochrome P450 and a 290x speedup for arcsin. The Lean library, problem specifications and verified solutions are open source, a useful template for anyone pairing agent search with formal checking.

evidence.quote: In a new paper , we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits.
For each problem, we tasked separate, independent agent teams with finding algorithmic improvements. These ideas were then verified with Lean, before entering a shared notebook.
Our agent teams cut the required computing cost (a metric that combines required qubits and operations) by 11.8×, and lowered required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits .
For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most human medicines and is important for drug design, they found a 2.5× improvement
a 290x speedup for arcsin, a common routine that is used by many other quantum algorithms to load numbers into quantum states.
To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library , problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.

items.title: inclusionAI releases Ling-3.2-air: 124B total, 5.5B active parameters
items.summary: Ling-3.2-air is an open-weight, MIT-licensed hybrid-linear MoE model that shares the native multimodal architecture of Ling-3.0-flash-VL, with 124B total and 5.5B activated parameters. Compared with its predecessor, its AutomationBench-AA score rises from 15.7% to 61% and its Terminal-Bench 4.0 pass rate from 0% to 27%. SGLang is the recommended runtime, with a 256K-context recipe on 4× 141GB-class GPUs.

evidence.quote: We introduce Ling-3.2-air , an open-weight model that shares the same native multimodal architecture as Ling-3.0-flash-VL .
Compared with its predecessor, Ling-3.2-air shows stronger performance in workflow automation and reasoning over professional documents. Its AutomationBench-AA score rises from 15.7% to 61% ,
On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , its pass rate on terminal-based tasks rises from 0% to 27% .
Architecture Hybrid-linear MoE Parameter Scale Total 124B, Activated 5.5B
Recommended recipe with 256K context, on 4× 141GB-class GPUs (H20-3e / H200)

items.title: Thinking Machines opens TML-d24-varloop-research, a variable-loop model
items.summary: This variable-looped counterpart to Inkling 2 Mini runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers with shared weights a number of times chosen at inference, after training with 1 to 5 passes; it has 26.4B parameters and 3.4B active, with each extra pass adding about 1.0B effective active parameters. The roughly 20GB checkpoint ships in native NVFP4 and MXFP8, needs a single machine with at least 32GB of GPU or unified memory, and is Apache 2.0, open weights only with no API. One set of weights makes it a clean testbed for how extra looped compute changes capability.

evidence.quote: It is a variable-looped counterpart to Inkling 2 Mini: whereas Inkling 2 Mini always runs its looped layers a fixed number of times, the number of loops in this model can be chosen at inference time. We are releasing it with open weights to support research on looped models.
Model provider: Thinking Machines Lab, Inc.

A 24-layer decoder-only transformer with sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feed-forward layers. The middle 12 layers run a variable number of times with shared weights, chosen at inference time; the model was trained with 1 to 5 passes.
Parameters 26.4B, 3.4B active Note: each extra pass through the looped layers adds about 1.0B effective active parameters per token.

The model is distributed as a single checkpoint of about 20GB. Its expert layers are NVFP4, the last four use MXFP8, and the remaining weights are BF16. The checkpoint requires a single machine with at least 32GB of GPU or unified memory.
The model is not available through an API, including Tinker. It is distributed as open weights only.
License: Apache 2.0

items.title: MemOnce shrinks the memory state cache 1313× at 1M context
items.summary: MemOnce caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory, decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers, and retrieves relevant memories with sparse indices computed once across layers, giving linear-time complexity. Adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce cuts the memory state cache by 1313× and prefill latency by 6.9× at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5×. For long-horizon agents and continual chat, it suggests a post-training path to much smaller KV caches.

evidence.quote: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers;
(b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers.

items.title: NoPeWorld reads DiT hidden states to stop objects passing through walls
items.summary: The authors' NoPeBench shows that no open-source interactive video world model reliably prevents object penetration, yet diffusion transformer hidden states already predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. NoPeWorld trains a small head on a frozen DiT and swaps unsafe actions for safe ones that preserve intent, cutting the average physical violation rate across six video world models from 74% to 16%. Code, benchmark and weights are released, making it a lightweight add-on for world-model and embodied-simulation work.

evidence.quote: Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations.

Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent.
NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%.
We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights.

items.title: cmHC balances residual stream mixing in hyper-connections
items.summary: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections keep stream-mixing matrices in the Birkhoff polytope; the paper shows under-mixing makes streams nearly independent, while over-mixing makes them hard to tell apart. cmHC geometrically contracts the polytope toward its interior with no new parameterization, plus a moderate contraction in shallow layers, for stable gradients in very large pretraining; fused operators on Ascend NPUs cut hyper-connection latency by up to 44.8%. Teams experimenting with multi-stream residuals get a tuning method with a provable mixing bound.

evidence.quote: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams;
when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other.
This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization.
Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining.
We also develop fused operators for cmHC on Ascend NPUs, reducing hyper-connection execution latency by up to 44.8%.

items.title: Ai2 releases RoboTrack: a point-tracking benchmark, data and models for robots
items.summary: RoboTrack-Bench has 307 human-annotated real manipulation videos, and leading trackers score much lower on it than on existing robotics benchmarks; RoboTrack-15M is a synthetic training set generated with Ai2's MolmoSpaces simulation ecosystem. Ai2 also released two trackers, RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp, and in a wet-lab test point tracking completed 17 of 20 transfers versus 8 for object masks. Teams that auto-label robot video with off-the-shelf trackers can use the benchmark to check them first.

evidence.quote: RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2 , and EgoVerse,
This pipeline produces RoboTrack-15M , a new synthetic training dataset targeted toward robotic manipulation.
Our evaluations show that leading trackers score much lower on RoboTrack-Bench than on existing robotics benchmarks.
Today, we’re releasing both RoboTrack components and two new point tracking models: RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp .
Point tracking completed the full transfer in 17 of 20 trials, compared with 8 for object masks and 5 for optical flow.
we also extend MolmoSpaces , Ai2’s simulation ecosystem for robot learning, to generate dense point tracks from simulated robot manipulation trajectories.

items.title: Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards enter public beta with zero data retention
items.summary: EFS detects misuse patterns across many requests by analyzing data on customer-controlled infrastructure, so neither Anthropic nor cloud providers retain it, on the Claude Platform, Amazon Bedrock, Claude on Google Cloud and more.

evidence.quote: Now, we're opening up EFS in public beta.
EFS provides state-of-the-art detection of sophisticated misuse, while remaining compatible with zero data retention (ZDR): neither Anthropic nor any cloud providers retain enterprises' data.
This layer looks for patterns of misuse across many requests.
Instead, our automated safety monitoring system analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by our customers.
EFS is available on the Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud.

items.title: Anthropic interviews 58 companies: few AI layoffs, but less hiring
items.summary: People at two-thirds of the companies reported reduced hiring due to AI, and the most valuable uses often involved reorganizing roles and workplaces around it.

evidence.quote: we conducted 66 interviews with 58 of Anthropic’s enterprise customers.
People at two-thirds of the companies we spoke to reported reduced hiring due to AI: as one person put it, “We may not be firing, but we’re not hiring.”

items.title: Hugging Face publishes a guide to building and maintaining agentic evals
items.summary: It recommends adapting an existing task, grading the saved output or final environment state rather than the agent's claim, reading traces, and reporting both pass@k and pass^k.

evidence.quote: pass@k asks whether at least one of k rollouts succeeds.
pass^k asks whether all k rollouts succeed.
Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation.
Grade what the agent produced: inspect the saved output, not its claim to have finished.
Verifier: The code that grades a rollout by checking the saved output or the environment's final state.
We work through eight steps: define the claim , find a task , run it unchanged , adapt it , check the evaluation , read the traces , report the score , and compare models .
